selection.reason: No candidate naturally completed every checkpoint 1 through 4 before action 32. The frozen screen therefore cannot supply three identified recursive feedback updates.

evidence: GLM-5 remained flat through ten same-task layers despite 30 accumulated references and 11.46x matching-control input load.
DeepSeek cumulative self-report reached ten same-task layers with isolated catastrophic workers at layers 2 and 7, but recovered completely on the next layer and ended at its best score.
DeepSeek recursive manager synthesis reached a near-textual fixed point by layer 3 and showed only a 0.018 mean decline from its earlier best by layer 5.

The new four-checkpoint screen failed because baseline agents became action-boundary censored before three feedback updates were available, not because a long valid feedback chain stayed untested on those tasks.
iteration_hypothesis.scientific_conclusion: Too few iterations remains a narrow delayed-threshold possibility, but current evidence makes it an unlikely general explanation for the missing sustained degradation curve. Increasing evolving-task checkpoints under the same fixed budget confounds iteration depth with baseline task infeasibility.
iteration_hypothesis.clean_remaining_test: If pursued, hold one real task and its evaluator fixed while extending only recursive manager updates to a prospectively frozen 10-to-12-layer run. Do not increase checkpoint difficulty, relax the action budget, or select a failed bootstrap source after outcomes.
